lessons.title: Synthesis — reading a paragraph
lessons.gloss: a whole paragraph you were never taught, read with eight endings and a handful of sound laws

segments.text: Decode estación. (Station — the e- off the front, the -ción to -tion at the back.)
Read it slowly. Not one of these words appears anywhere else in this book.
La comunidad literaria tiene una tradición extraordinaria. Su estructura es voluntaria, evidentemente, pero la actividad es enorme.

utterances: what you saw: comunidad. how you got it: -dad becomes -ty.
what you saw: literaria. how you got it: -ario, agreeing becomes -ary.
what you saw: tradición. how you got it: -ción becomes -tion.
what you saw: extraordinaria. how you got it: -ario, agreeing becomes -ary.
what you saw: estructura. how you got it: take the e- off becomes structure.
what you saw: voluntaria. how you got it: -ario, agreeing becomes -ary.
what you saw: evidentemente. how you got it: -mente becomes -ly.
what you saw: actividad. how you got it: -dad becomes -ty.

segments.text: The literary community has an extraordinary tradition. Its structure is voluntary, evidently, but the activity is enormous.
Nine words. Eight fell to rules you hold, and the ninth is below.
The endings were never the point. This is:

A paragraph of unfamiliar Spanish is no longer a wall. Most of it is words you already know, wearing clothes you have learned to recognise. That change of expectation is worth more than any single word, because it is what lets you read above your level and get most of it — which is how the rest of the language arrives.

Enorme is the ninth, and no ending gives it to you. You guessed it anyway, from enormous, and the guess was right. That is what the rules are really for: they do not decode every word, they make the guessing safe.

segments.instruction: the paragraph, out loud, all of it
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the paragraph, out loud, all of it]

segments.prompt: Decode: la comunidad tiene una tradicion.

feedback.correct: Two endings, one sentence, nothing memorised.

segments.prompt: Decode: su estructura es voluntaria, evidentemente.
A word you have never seen: especialista. What is it?

feedback.correct: The e- came off and -ista became -ist. Two rules, one word.
feedback.incorrect: A specialist — e- off the front, -ista to -ist.

segments.text: How many of those words appear anywhere else in this book? (None.) How many did you read? (All of them.) And what is the real change? (An unfamiliar paragraph is no longer a wall.)
